source.standardization: b * sampleSD(X) / sampleSD(sales), using observations 2-24; not causal importance or variance explained

'Model output'!A2.value: sales = a + b1·prom + b2·adv + b3·prom_lag1 + b4·adv_lag1 + b5·index + b6·cold    (23 quarters, $ thousands)

'Model output'!J3.value: Helper: raw LINEST output (coefficients run right-to-left: cold, index, adv_lag1, prom_lag1, adv, prom, intercept)

'Model output'!A26.value: Net sales per $1k of advertising, over two quarters ($k)

'Model output'!A27.value: Net sales per $1k of promotion, over two quarters ($k)

'Model output'!A33.value: Break-even margin = 1 / net sales per $1 spent (Session 4: profit per $1 = margin × slope − 1). The case gives no margin, so this is the threshold, not a profit estimate.

'Data'!N2.value: Blue = original case data (Qkitch.xlsx), in $ thousands except index and the quarter dummies.

'Data'!N3.value: prom_lag1 / adv_lag1 = promotion / advertising spent in the previous quarter (empty for quarter 1).

'Data'!N4.value: cold = 1 in Q1 or Q4 (the colder quarters), 0 otherwise. Assumes q1 = January to March.

'Regression input'!L2.value: 1. Data tab > Data Analysis > Regression (enable the Analysis ToolPak add-in if it is missing).

'Regression input'!L3.value: 2. Input Y Range: B1:B24 (sales). Input X Range: C1:H24 (the six explanatory variables).

'Regression input'!L4.value: 3. Tick Labels, keep Confidence Level 95%, output to a new worksheet.

'Regression input'!L5.value: 4. The result should match the 'Model output' sheet, which computes the same regression live with LINEST.

'Regression input'!L6.value: Quarter 1 is left out because it has no previous quarter for the lagged variables (23 observations).
